div.head: II As 14.2
div.ab: On Cantwarabyrig VII myneteras: IIII ðæs cynges ⁊ II (þæs) biscopes, I ðæs abbodes; to Hrofeceastre: II cynges ⁊ I (þæs) biscopes; to Lundenbyrig VIII; to Wintaceastre VI; to Læwe II; to Hæstingaceastre I; oþer to Cisseceastre; to Hamtune II; to Wærham II; to Execeastre II; to Sceaftesbyrig II; elles to þam oþrum burgum I.

On Cantwarabyrig VII myneteras: IIII cynges, II bisceopes ⁊ án ðæs abbodes; to Hrofeceastre III: twegen þæs cynges ⁊ an ðæs bisceopes; to Lundenbyrig VIII; to Winteceastre VI; to Læwes II; to Hæstingaceastre I; oþer to Cysseceastre; to Hamtun twegen; to Werham II; twegen to Eaxanceastre; II to Sceaftesbyrig; elles to ðæm oþrum burgum an.

On [Cant]warabyrg VII mynetras: IIII cinges, II bisceopes [⁊ I þæs] abbodes; to Rofeceastre III: twegen þæs cinges ⁊ [án þæs bi]scopes; to Lundenbyrg VIII; to Winteceastre VI; to [Læwe I]I; to Hæstingaceastre I; oþer to Cysseceastre; [to Ham]tune twegen; twegen to Werham; twegen to Æxeceastre; [twegen to Sce]aftesbyrg; elles to þam oðrum burgum án.

In Cantuaria septem monetarii sint: regis quatuor, episcopi duo, abbatis unus; in Rouecestria tres: regis duo, episcopi unus; in Lundonia VIII; in Wintonia VI; in Lewis II; in Hastingecestre unus; in Cicestria (Cirecestre) unus; in Hamtune duo; in Warham duo; in Dorchecestre unus; in Sceaftesberi duo; in Exonia duo; et in aliis burgis unus.

On Cantwarabyrig VII myneteras: IIII þæs cynges ⁊ II þæs biscopes I ðæs abbodes; to Hrofeceastre [III]: II cynges ⁊ I þæs biscopes to Lundenbyrig VIII; to Wintaceastre VI; to Læwe II; to Hæstingaceastre I; oþer to Cisseceastre; to Hamtune II: to Wærham II; [to Dorcaceastre I]; to Execeastre II; to Sceaftesbyrig II; elles to þam oðrum burgum I.

In Canterbury [seien] 7 Münzer: 4 des Königs und 2 des [Erz-]Bischofs, 1 des Abts [von St. Austins]; zu Rochester (3 Ot Ld): 2 des Königs und 1 des Bischofs; zu London 8; zu Winchester 6; zu Lewes 2; zu Hastings 1; ein zweiter zu Chichester; zu Southampton 2; zu Wareham 2; (zu Dorchester 1 So); zu Exeter 2; zu Shaftesbury 2; sonst in den anderen Burg-Städten [je] 1.

In Canterbury [let there be] 7 moneyers: 4 of the king and 2 of the [arch]bishop, 1 of the abbot [of St Augustine's]; at Rochester (3, Ot Ld): 2 of the king and 1 of the bishop; at London 8; at Winchester 6; at Lewes 2; at Hastings 1; another at Chichester; at Southampton 2; at Wareham 2; (at Dorchester 1, So); at Exeter 2; at Shaftesbury 2; otherwise in the other boroughs 1 [each].

In Canterbury there shall be seven moneyers: four for the king, two for the archbishop, one for the abbot. In Rochester, two for the king and one for the bishop. In London eight; in Winchester six; in Lewes two; in Hastings one; another in Chichester; two in Southampton; two in Wareham; [one in Dorchester]; two in Exeter; two at Shaftesbury, and one in [each of] the other boroughs.

In Canterbury [there are to be] seven moneyers; four of the king, two of the bishop, one of the abbot; in Rochester three, two of the king, one of the bishop; in London eight; in Winchester six; in Lewes two; in Hastings one; another at Chichester; at Southampton two; at Wareham two; [at Dorchester one]; at Exeter two; at Shaftesbury two; otherwise in the other boroughs one.
div.note: So adds ‘to Dorceceaster I’; Liebermann would supply it from So and Quadr. In H, ‘III’ is to be supplied for Rochester from Ot, Ld and Quadr. So breaks off after this chapter.

Alle hier genannten Orte hatten Münzen unter Æthelstan und um 1060; Willet in Numism. chron. 16 (1876) 373; Ellis Introd. to Domesday I 175. Viele andere Münzstädte Æthelstans (Ballard Engl. borough 12. cty 43) mag dieser unter denen mit nur Einem Münzer meinen. Dieser König prägte zuerst auch anderwärts als bloss in alten Römerstädten (Ballard 73). Aber auch York, Derby, Leicester, Norwich (vgl. Henfrey in Jl. Brit. archl. assoc. 1880, 302) zeigen 3—12 verschiedene Münzernamen, die freilich nicht gleichzeitig zu sein brauchen; Rossi in Notizie degli scavi 1883, 505. Vgl. jetzt A. Anscombe Names of Old-Engl. mint-towns in Brit. numism. jl. 8. 9, 1912/13

All the places named here had mints under Æthelstan and c. 1060; Willet in Numism. chron. 16 (1876) 373; Ellis Introd. to Domesday I 175. Many other mint towns of Æthelstan (Ballard Engl. borough 12. cty 43) he may mean among those with only one moneyer. This king was also the first to coin elsewhere than merely in old Roman towns (Ballard 73). But York, Derby, Leicester, Norwich too (cf. Henfrey in Jl. Brit. archl. assoc. 1880, 302) show 3—12 different moneyers’ names, which, however, need not be contemporaneous; Rossi in Notizie degli scavi 1883, 505. Cf. now A. Anscombe Names of Old-Engl. mint-towns in Brit. numism. jl. 8. 9, 1912/13
Vgl. Gl Feiertag 8 d: Dunstans Strafjustiz über Münzfälscher in Canterbury. — Dortige Münzen s. Powell in Engl. hist. rev. 1896, 765; Rossi 505. 514 mit drei verschiedenen Münzernamen
Cf. Gl Feiertag 8 d: Dunstan’s punitive justice against coiners at Canterbury. — For coins from there see Powell in Engl. hist. rev. 1896, 765; Rossi 505. 514, with three different moneyers’ names
In Grossstadt 3, sonst nur 1 belässt dagegen IV Atr 9
IV Atr 9, by contrast, leaves 3 in a large town and otherwise only 1
Vgl. Powell 759. Kent und London, die grösste Handelsstadt, gehen Wessex voran; noch zweimal u. Erkl. 8. 11 wird nach Grafschaften geordnet
Cf. Powell 759. Kent and London, the largest commercial town, precede Wessex; twice more, below notes 8. 11, the order is by shires
London (s. d. Gl 43) hat die meisten, wirtschaftlicher Bedeutung gemäss
London (see that word in Gl 43) has the most, in keeping with its economic importance
Die andere Stadt Hampshires folgt erst nach drei anderen
The other town of Hampshire follows only after three others

Drei in Sussex hintereinander (über die Münze in Hastings vgl. Powell 765; Burrows Cinque ports 25); aus ihnen und Rochester kennt keine Münze Æthelstans Keary Catal. of Ags. coins II p. cix, wohl aber ein wenig spätere

Three in Sussex in succession (on the mint at Hastings cf. Powell 765; Burrows Cinque ports 25); Keary Catal. of Ags. coins II p. cix knows no coin of Æthelstan from them or from Rochester, but does know somewhat later ones
Um 1050—60 hatte Chichester eine Münze; Ellis 175; Numism. chron. 19, 155. — ‘Cirencester’ verderbt nur Q ii; dort, in Gloucestershire, ist keine Münze Æthelstans bekannt
About 1050—60 Chichester had a mint; Ellis 175; Numism. chron. 19, 155. — ‘Cirencester’ is a corruption only in Q ii; no coin of Æthelstan is known from there, in Gloucestershire

Dass As mit Hamtun nicht Northampton meine, ergibt Zusammenhang; doch stammen dorther manche der mit Hamtun bezeichneten Münzen; Stevenson in EHR 1899, 590. ‘Southampton’ erklärt hier Keary II p. cxv. — Zu Wareham in Dorset ward um 1050 gemünzt

That As does not mean Northampton by Hamtun follows from the context; yet some of the coins marked Hamtun do come from there; Stevenson in EHR 1899, 590. Keary II p. cxv interprets it here as ‘Southampton’. — Coins were struck at Wareham in Dorset c. 1050

Den Zusatz führte entweder sq ein, oder er ist archetyp und sowohl von Ot wie von hb nur übersprungen, fehlt daher in II und uns verlorenem, von Ld hier vielleicht befolgtem, Kodex B. Dem Stammbaume nach wäre (wenn nicht die 3 Worte etwa am Rande des Archetyps standen) ersteres, dem Sinne nach ist letzteres wahrscheinlicher, denn dann stehen zwei Prägestätten Dorsets beieinander. — Münzen Æthelstans mit Dor. civit. zeigen 5 verschiedene Münzer

The addition was either introduced by sq, or it belongs to the archetype and was merely skipped by both Ot and hb, and is therefore missing in II and in the codex B lost to us, which Ld perhaps followed here. On the stemma the former would be more probable (unless the 3 words perhaps stood in the margin of the archetype), on the sense the latter, for then two mints of Dorset stand side by side. — Coins of Æthelstan with Dor. civit. show 5 different moneyers
Als Prägeorte bei Powell. Nur späte Hss. des Q verderben: Salisbury, Oxford, aus welchen Städten allerdings auch Agsächs. Münzen existieren
As mints in Powell. Only late MSS of Q corrupt it to Salisbury, Oxford, from which towns, it is true, Anglo-Saxon coins also exist
Nicht ‘Burg’; über die Identität mit port s. Gl Stadt 1. 2; Maitland Domesday 195. — Vgl. o.⁸
Not ‘fortress’; on the identity with port see Gl Stadt 1. 2; Maitland Domesday 195. — Cf. above⁸

Athelstan’s coins commonly bear the name of the place where they were minted. Of the boroughs here mentioned, London, Winchester, Wareham, Exeter, along with 14 other boroughs, are represented in the Brit. Mus. Catalogue of English Coins (vol. ii. p. 105 ff.).
